B-historical-evidence.json.evidence: Museum evidence supports tunics, belts and woven decoration in Byzantine clothing; use restrained riding-length clothes and boots. Barbara Schrodt, Journal of Sport History8/3(1981), Sports of the Byzantine Empire, quotes Cinnamus describing netted-loop sticks for mounted tzykanion.
B-historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Exact tenth-century sports clothing and equipment are not preserved as a full ensemble; netted-loop description is a later Byzantine source used as cautious reconstruction. Palace field layout and facades are interpretive.

historical-evidence.json.evidence: Palace complex extended across descending terraces; tenth-century ceremonial core included octagonal domed Chrysotriklinos with surrounding vaulted halls. Low palace wings, courtyards and palatine chapels are synthesized into a compact map symbol.
historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Lost complex: precise overall ground plan, roof forms, facades and building-to-building arrangement are uncertain. Image is an interpretive reconstruction, not an archaeological exact-plan model.

B-historical-evidence.json.evidence: Met museum essay explains sticharion, phelonion and priestly stole, distinguishing later elaborate vestments. Turkish Directorate General of Cultural Assets and Museums documents porphyry imperial sarcophagi, plain sides, pitched lids, wreath-and-cross carving and their Holy Apostles provenance.
B-historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Exact tomb placement and church interior are lost; the scene uses an adjoining imperial burial area with a plausible view into the domed church. Sarcophagi are not assigned to named emperors. Five-domed building does not imply all five domes can physically be visible in one photograph.

historical-evidence.json.evidence: Dumbarton Oaks documents Underwood/Friend/Downey reconstruction research using written sources and comparative buildings; academic Harvard exhibition identifies cruciform five-domed form.
historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Destroyed church; reconstruction details and tenth-century drum changes remain uncertain. Five-dome cruciform silhouette is prioritized over speculative facade precision. Explicitly exclude Athens Holy Apostles: Apostoliki Diakonia item10 was checked and describes the different Athens church, not used.

B-historical-evidence.json.evidence: Royal Ontario Museum and FIT document purple/gold toga picta for triumphal dress; Capitoline Museums preserve relief evidence for imperial ceremony and bull at the Jupiter temple. Architecture uses the documented hexastyle front/deep porch/high podium.
B-historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Narrative is the commissioned c100CE type scene, not a claim to reconstruct a specific recorded triumph. Architectural decoration, procession positions and clothing detail are interpretive. Later Marcus Aurelius relief supports ceremonial type, not exact AD100 identity.

historical-evidence.json.evidence: Capitoline Museums describe high podium, frontal stairs, colonnades on three sides, deep porch with two additional front rows and three cellae. Rome tourism specifies six front columns. AD100 corresponds to the rebuilt Domitian-era marble temple.
historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Exact decorative details, color distribution and roof ornaments are reconstructed; later reliefs simplify the column count. Image follows architectural hexastyle reconstruction, not the relief shorthand.
